facts_from_discussion: The court found, on the basis of a copy of the 2015 Form 1040 and the related IRS account transcript, that a joint 2015 tax return was filed by Ms. Kapoor and her husband, Mr. Escamilla. Petitioner neither claimed nor produced any evidence that his daughter's marriage or her joint 2015 Form 1040 is invalid.
I.M.E. and P.A.E. are petitioner's grandchildren and Ms. Kapoor's children.

I.M.E. and P.A.E. had the same principal place of abode as both petitioner and Ms. Kapoor for more than one-half of 2015; P.A.E. was born in fall 2015 and lived with petitioner and Ms. Kapoor for the remainder of the year.
I.M.E. and P.A.E. were minors during 2015, did not provide more than one-half of their own support for 2015, and neither child was married or filed a joint return for 2015.
Both petitioner and Ms. Kapoor claimed I.M.E. and P.A.E. as dependents on their 2015 returns.
Petitioner was not aware that his daughter filed a joint tax return with her spouse for 2015.
As reported on his amended return, petitioner's adjusted gross income and earned income for 2015 both exceeded $14,820.
